entries.why_wrong: That would only skip `items[0]`, which was never the problem — the loop already starts correctly at `i = 0`. The actual issue is at the top end: `range(len(items) + 1)` lets `i` reach `len(items)`, an index that doesn't exist.

Shifting to `items[i - 1]` just moves which element crashes instead of removing the crash — the loop would still run one iteration too many because `range()` still goes up to `len(items)`. The fix has to shrink the range itself, not offset the index used inside it.

The loop does print the first element fine, since `i` starts at 0 and `items[0]` is valid. The real failure happens on the last iteration, when `i` reaches `len(items)` and indexes one past the end of the list.
